summary: Hexagonal-prism tumbler, version 5: one rigid hexagonal body (circumradius 25.5 mm) that rolls over its hexagon edges onto face F3 (rest orientation 180 deg about y, lobe parked at body -z), driven by an internal lift ring with one lobe (geared from a 6 mm gearmotor, 304 internal-gear band in a PA12 carrier); axial couplers on the two end faces: a machined 304 hex peg on the head (6.5 mm engagement), and a tail receiver with a roll-in channel (two arcs through the F3 bottom vertices), a yaw turntable whose 304 collar bears on a concave 304 saddle (cylindrical thrust face coaxial with the yaw axis), a flat 304 seat and a 304 three-flat jaw that closes to a fixed height with a declared vertical gap, and a motor-driven over-centre four-bar keeper whose pivot, crank stops, M3 bearing, saddle and base are one machined 304 frame (third gearmotor, no SMA, no spring). BLE only, no power transfer.

assembly_access.statement: Walls and end plates are separate PA12 parts joined by two PA12 axial posts (from y -6.9 to the head end plate) and four M1.6 screws (screw positions are a lumped stand-in). The V-shaped roll-in channel cuts end plate b and the tail cap into three pieces; the keeper frame (304) is fixed to the middle triangle piece and its saddle insert sits in a window of that piece. Each wall half (head and tail) is a separate part so the lift ring can be dropped into the girdle slot between them. The cell, controller and boards load as a stack along the axis with one end plate removed; the head peg installs from the head end plate and the tail receiver parts (puck, collar, seat web, keeper tongue, jaw and rod) install from the tail end. M3 is a column in the vacated left interior slot with its frame bearing block standing on end plate b; M2 is the right interior column. No assembly sequence has been verified; the gear train, yaw worm, four-bar routing, the puck-to-collar joint and the press fits are not shown to be assemblable.

retention.mechanism: The head peg's annular groove (dia 3.0 x 1.4 wide, groove centre at A-frame y 27.1 = 5.1 mm inside the neighbour's face; engagement 6.5 mm, tip y 28.5) is closed from above (body +z) by a 1.0 mm 304 keeper tongue (B frame y -9.4 to -8.4) whose closed lower edge is on the receiver axis (z 0.0) with a semicircular notch r 1.55. Groove engagement (single value, corrected hexagon test): the plate overlaps the peg shoulder between the groove root (r 1.5) and the hex over 3.04 mm2 with the peg axis on the tongue axis; the area falls to 0.14 mm2 if the peg sits 0.9 mm low in the vertical free play (3.41 mm2 at +0.15). Tension path (design tension 4 mu W = 1.683 N, mu 1 provisional): peg shoulder, tongue, stem (2 x 2) in the PA12 guide slot of the puck column, puck column, 304 puck collar (joint not designed), concave 304 saddle insert of the keeper frame (cylindrical thrust face, collar r 3.8 on saddle r 4.2, line contact 1.4 mm), end plate b middle piece, F3 wall. v5 has no washer. The tongue is moved by a motor-driven over-centre four-bar: crank r 2.0 on the M3 axis (-4.500, 12.272), link 10.216 mm, rocker pivot (5.250, 15.322) (link-side arm 3.0, output arm 4.5), push rod on the yaw axis through the hollow yaw shaft, pin-in-slot yoke bar. The pivot post, the two stop lugs, the M3 bearing block, the saddle and the rod guide (the shaft bore) are on ONE machined 304 frame part (base plate 0.6 mm on the middle triangle piece), so the lock geometry carries only class-f machining tolerance (ISO 2768-1 f: +-0.05 mm to 6 mm, +-0.1 mm 6 to 30 mm). Two stable geometric states: CLOSED = crank 10 deg past the folded dead centre against a hard stop, OPEN = 10 deg past the extended dead centre against a second stop (the crank travels 202.5 deg, the rocker 82.6 deg, the rod 5.58 mm for 4.6 mm needed). Link line offset from the crank axis 0.277 mm closed, 0.422 mm open. Declared tolerance basis (size rule, 1 024 corners): margin past the dead centre at least 5.64 deg open / 6.09 deg closed, rod stroke 5.088 to 6.068 mm; with every frame coordinate +-0.1: 5.19 / 5.41 deg, 5.035 to 6.113 mm; frame plus bearing and pin play (C and Pv +-0.15, L +-0.2, r b a +-0.1): 1.73 / 3.59 deg, 4.631 to 6.613 mm (margins stay positive, stroke stays at least 4.6 mm). Vertical stack: the jaw closes to a FIXED height set by the crank stop on the frame; it does not seat on the seat and no jaw-to-peg contact is required (no flexure; the jaw entry chamfer 0.6 x 30 deg is a seating lead-in only). Vertical gap (free play P between the seat top and the jaw top flat, less the peg across-flats): nominal 0.55 mm; worst case 0.05 to 1.05 mm = nominal +-0.35 (unit-to-unit stack: both units' SLS +-0.3 plus the PA12 chain frame-end plate-puck-seat, stated by the lead) +-0.05 jaw flat, +-0.05 seat top, +-0.05 peg across flats (class f, arithmetic sum). Lateral clearance per flat 0.10 nominal (pocket AF 4.20 +-0.05 against peg AF 4.00 +-0.05: 0.05 to 0.15). Jaw and seat modelled as exact polygons, peg hex AF 4.0, configuration space (x, z, roll) searched on a 0.05 mm / 1 deg grid (0.01 mm / 0.5 deg for the tight corner) from the seated pose: tight corner (P 0.05): z span 0.05, x +-0.05, roll lash +-0.5 deg; nominal (P 0.55): z -0.45 to +0.10, x +-0.35, roll lash +-12 deg; loose corner (P 1.05): z -0.90 to +0.15, x +-0.65, roll free over the full +-30 deg (the 60 deg hex period), i.e. NO roll lock at the loose corner. No state reachable in any of the three cases leaves |x| or |z| > 7 mm: with the jaw closed the peg cannot leave along either arc or sideways or up or down (the lower sides are open but the 4.0 mm hex does not fit the 2.45 mm opening between the seat top and the leg lower edge unless it is rolled 30 deg, which needs P > 0.62 and then the legs and ceiling still block it). Only the jaw and seat are in this model; the tongue additionally blocks the pull-out in y. Load-reversal at the dead centre as in v4 (pin friction bound recomputed in the dossier). Nothing is powered to hold.

release.means: The unit's own keeper motor M3 (Precision Microdrives 206-109 via driver-2) drives the crank over the dead centres: 203 deg from the closed stop to the open stop, retracting the tongue by 5.58 mm (4.6 mm needed with the tongue closing at z 0.0). The open state is held geometrically by the second stop. Release friction counts both faces under the chain tension T: the peg shoulder on the tongue and the stem on the guide slot wall, each normal force T at the friction bound mu 1 (provisional), so the force on the rod is 2 mu T and the crank torque is 2 mu T x 2.871 mm/rad (peak lever). Operating rule: release only when the chain tension is at most T_rel = 3 mN m / (2 mu x 2.871) = 0.522 N (1.24 W, 31% of the design tension 4 mu W = 1.683 N), so that the M3 rated torque suffices (stall: 1.567 N). At the full mu = 1 bound tension 1.683 N release needs 9.66 mN m = 1.07 x M3 stall (9 mN m): release is blocked at that bound (CPL-008 allows blocked release); the controller relaxes the chain tension first. Docking sequence: open keeper (M3), roll in, IMU detects landing, close keeper (M3). It acts only on this unit's own receiver. Crank stop wear, M3 heat and cycle life are UNRESOLVED.

alignment.description: Roll-in channel from the corrected roll kinematics: two circular-arc slots, radius 25.5 mm, centred on the two F3 bottom vertices (+-12.75, +22.084), running from the vertices to the face centre (a V opening toward +z), 5.8 mm wide, 7.0 mm deep from the tail face, 45 deg x 1.5 mm flared mouths; end plate b slot +-4.545 x +-2.6 mm at the centre.
alignment.justification: Table-height condition (world frame, A fixed, B resting on F3 and rolling from one step to the side about the shared bottom edge P): the peg point lies in B's frame on the circle of radius 25.5 about B's bottom vertex, from B's other bottom vertex (roll 0) to the face centre (roll 60 deg); B's lowest vertex stays on the table, its centre rises to 25.5 mm at 30 deg of roll; the peg hex turns 60 deg relative to B. The final approach is along 30 deg from the body x axis. Slot width 5.8 mm (4.619 + 2 x 0.59) gives 0.59 mm per side nominal, minimum slot 5.5 mm (SLS +-0.3% with a lower limit of +-0.3 mm, Materialise PA12 SLS, https://www.materialise.com/en/industrial/3d-printing-materials/pa12-sls) 0.44 mm per side. Windows AT THE SLOT: lateral at the mouth +-(0.59+1.5) = +-2.09 mm (min +-1.94); height +-0.59 (min +-0.44); heading (two-point jam, engagement 6.5 mm) 11.3 deg nominal, 8.2 deg at the SLS minimum slot and 7.6 deg with the peg at the class-f upper limit; roll any multiple of 60 deg; axial +-0.5 mm. WINDOWS AT THE JAW (open jaw, swept hex AF 4.0, jaw outer block x +-2.9): height margin toward the jaw 0.448 mm at the nominal stroke 5.582, 0.104 mm at the size-rule class-f minimum stroke 5.088, 0.052 mm at 5.035 (every coordinate +-0.1), 0.000 mm at the frame-plus-play minimum 4.631; for the tongue 1.025 / 0.654 / 0.614 / 0.318 mm. These are for a peg at the nominal height: they take no allowance for the peg-height offset (up to +-0.6 mm, both units' SLS +-0.3) and no allowance for the +-0.35 mm stack between the seat and the frame, so the jaw window toward the jaw is REDUCED-MARGIN and is not closed. THERE IS NO AXIAL OR HEADING PRE-ALIGNMENT MEANS other than these windows, and a free approach cannot start a roll-in: docking needs B one roll step to the side in a common lane (axial inside +-0.5 mm, heading inside the window, the peg already engaged 6.5 mm), only reachable by rolling out of a previous dock. Nominal geometric estimates; the capture window is not claimed (CPL-006). No magnet and no cone.

alignment.description: Tongue seating feature (not a pre-alignment means): semicircular notch r 1.55 with a 30 deg half-angle lead-in wedge (0.3 mm each side, tip face 0.4 mm) that seats the groove root as the crank closes.
alignment.justification: The V-notch of v3 is not a declared pre-alignment means: with flank friction 0.15 the lateral push fraction is 0.393, so the rated closing force 1.04 N gives 0.41 N against mu W = 0.421 N at mu 1: ratio 0.98 (stall 2.93), below the 1.5 rule. The notch seats a peg already inside the channel window; with the vertical free play the peg may sit up to 0.9 mm low and then the notch does not wrap the groove root at all (overlap 0.14 mm2); the tongue retains the peg by the shoulder overlap only. The tongue is driven by M3 through the four-bar, not by a spring.

alignment.description: Hex peg in a flat seat and a three-flat jaw that closes to a fixed height, with the vertical free play declared; 0.5 x 45 deg tip chamfer on the peg and a 0.6 x 30 deg lead-in chamfer on the jaw.
alignment.justification: The hexagonal peg (4.0 mm across flats) has six equivalent roll positions; the receiver is a flat seat (top at nominal z -2.45) below the peg and a jaw (pocket AF 4.20, upper flat at z +2.10) that closes from above after landing to a height fixed by the crank stop on the frame. The seat is NOT registered to the frame (it stays on the PA12 puck web / end plate piece), so the free play is a declared quantity: Vertical gap (free play P between the seat top and the jaw top flat, less the peg across-flats): nominal 0.55 mm; worst case 0.05 to 1.05 mm = nominal +-0.35 (unit-to-unit stack: both units' SLS +-0.3 plus the PA12 chain frame-end plate-puck-seat, stated by the lead) +-0.05 jaw flat, +-0.05 seat top, +-0.05 peg across flats (class f, arithmetic sum). Lateral clearance per flat 0.10 nominal (pocket AF 4.20 +-0.05 against peg AF 4.00 +-0.05: 0.05 to 0.15). Jaw and seat modelled as exact polygons, peg hex AF 4.0, configuration space (x, z, roll) searched on a 0.05 mm / 1 deg grid (0.01 mm / 0.5 deg for the tight corner) from the seated pose: tight corner (P 0.05): z span 0.05, x +-0.05, roll lash +-0.5 deg; nominal (P 0.55): z -0.45 to +0.10, x +-0.35, roll lash +-12 deg; loose corner (P 1.05): z -0.90 to +0.15, x +-0.65, roll free over the full +-30 deg (the 60 deg hex period), i.e. NO roll lock at the loose corner. No state reachable in any of the three cases leaves |x| or |z| > 7 mm: with the jaw closed the peg cannot leave along either arc or sideways or up or down (the lower sides are open but the 4.0 mm hex does not fit the 2.45 mm opening between the seat top and the leg lower edge unless it is rolled 30 deg, which needs P > 0.62 and then the legs and ceiling still block it). Only the jaw and seat are in this model; the tongue additionally blocks the pull-out in y. Roll lash and torsion with the gap: at the nominal gap the peg turns +-12 deg before three corner contacts (the two jaw inclined flats and the seat) lock it; equal normal forces F, torque = 2.141 mm x F, so one idle neighbour tipped (5.36 mN m) gives F = 2.51 N and two (10.73 mN m) F = 5.01 N; at the tight corner the pair is top-flat corner and seat corner with arm 2.302 mm (F = 2.33 / 4.66 N); at the loose corner (P 1.05) the peg turns freely and carries no roll torque. Cam-out on the jaw z axis = F (5.01 N for two neighbours) plus the pitch couple W/2 x 36 over 1.4 mm = 5.41 N (modelling assumption), combined 10.42 N, carried by the over-centre stop. Hertz p0 at the contacts (assumed 0.1 mm corner radius, line load F/1.4 mm): 791 MPa (one neighbour) and 1119 MPa (two) against the 342 MPa first-yield rule of thumb. No attractive force acts: a unit that is not driven does not self-dock.

limitations: Roll-in docking was checked on paper only (kinematics with the table-height condition and a swept-volume check); the dynamics (impact, whether the ring-driven roll lands inside the windows) and the capture window are UNRESOLVED. There is no axial or heading pre-alignment means, and a free approach cannot start a roll-in.
No steering or axial locomotion is provided: the body rolls only perpendicular to its axis.

Yaw bending works only while the chain rests on a face with a vertical yaw axis. Yaw torque margin at table mu = 1 is 0.94 at rated motor torque for the declared 42.905 g mass (27 T sector unchanged). The worm self-locks only if the worm/sector friction coefficient is at least 0.125 (UNRESOLVED).

Release: both friction faces counted (shoulder and stem slot, 2 mu T). At the full mu = 1 design tension 1.683 N it needs 9.66 mN m, 1.07 x M3 stall: blocked at that bound (CPL-008); the operating rule is release at tension <= T_rel = 0.522 N (1.24 W). Rod stroke 5.58 mm nominal, 5.088 to 6.068 mm in the size-rule corners. Pin and yoke-bar envelope corners exceed the r <= 20 packing rule by about 0.02 mm nominal and about 0.2 mm at the stroke corners.

Vertical stack: the +-0.35 mm stack (stated by the lead, not derived here) is not absorbed by any compliance (a 304 flexure was found infeasible: 0.7 mm range at 0.41 N stores 0.6 mJ, 50 to 130 mm3 of fully stressed spring); it becomes the declared free play P = 0.05 to 1.05 mm. Consequences: roll lash +-0.5 deg (tight) to +-12 deg (nominal) to none (loose, P > 0.62); the roll lock is therefore not a qualified function; the open-jaw clearance to the swept peg is 0.104 mm at the size-rule minimum stroke (0.052 and 0.000 mm in the wider cases) with no allowance for the peg height offset; the tongue overlap falls to 0.14 mm2 at 0.9 mm low. The seat is not registered to the frame. The escape check models the jaw and seat only.

Load reversal of the over-centre lock as in v4 (passive for single-sign loads; reversal at the dead centre needs pin friction, bound in the dossier; real friction not cited). M3 radial load = link force, up to 11.3 N (open) and 17.1 N (closed) at the combined tongue force 10.4 N; frame bearing (304, d 2.0 x L 2.4 = 4.8 mm2) pressure 2.3 and 3.6 MPa taking the whole link force; the M3 shaft material and the gearbox radial rating are not cited (UNRESOLVED). M3 body to frame alignment (the shaft is located by the frame bearing and by the gearbox bearings) is not designed. Remaining PA12 contacts (stem in the guide slot, seat web on the puck, rocker pin hole, puck column) have pressures listed in the dossier with no allowable claimed.

Thrust: 304 collar r 3.8 (3.75 to 3.85) on 304 saddle r 4.2 (4.15 to 4.25), line contact 1.4 mm, tension 1.683 N: Hertz p0 28 to 36 MPa (E* 109.9 GPa), against 304 yield 205 MPa (no PA12 in this contact). The collar-to-puck-column joint, the moment between the stem plane and the collar plane, the +y radial restraint of the collar (no rear ring: the layout has no room) and the saddle insert window in end plate b are not designed or are UNRESOLVED.

The frame is one machined 304 part only for the features on the middle triangle piece (M3 block, rocker post, saddle, base). The seat and the lower cap strips are on another end-plate piece and are NOT registered to it. The hardware that joins the middle triangle piece to the F3 wall and the screws are not designed.

Many masses are upper bounds from solid volumes (walls, end plates, caps, puck, peg, lobe, gear band, saddle insert partly in the end plate b box); end plate b is the full hexagon although the V cut, window and slot remove material; the placement of screws and harness is a lumped stand-in; boxes of the link, rocker, rod and yoke are envelopes of swept parts; the M3 shaft stub and the crank stop lugs are not boxed; the saddle and collar boxes are stand-ins for round parts. Hertz contact stress at the peg corners exceeds the first-yield rule of thumb (local indentation expected).

Gear teeth are integer: ring 133 T pitch r 19.95 (304 band) and pinion 14 T pitch r 2.1 (module 0.3, centre distance 17.85); spurs 41 T and 16 T at module 0.2; yaw worm 1 start into 27 teeth per turn at module 0.3. Tooth strength, backlash, profile and contact ratio are not assessed. The M1 group is rotated 60 deg about the ring axis from its v3 position.

Tolerances: SLS PA12 accuracy is cited from Materialise (https://www.materialise.com/en/industrial/3d-printing-materials/pa12-sls) as +-0.3% with a lower limit of +-0.3 mm and minimum wall 1 mm; machined 304 parts are specified ISO 2768-1 class f (https://amesweb.info/fits-tolerances/iso-2768-linear-dimensions-tolerances.aspx), +-0.05 mm for 0.5 to 6 mm and +-0.1 mm for 6 to 30 mm. Materialise is a service-provider page, not EOS PA 2200 material data. Thin features below 0.5 mm are outside the cited table. Heat is not assessed.

The Precision Microdrives 206-109 datasheet is headed as a sampling/target specification; the three motors run from 3.7 V by PWM limited to 3.0 V effective, a control constraint. The datasheet gives no radial shaft load rating, which the crank link and the worm load.

The QT Py regulator is rated 600 mA peak; the 2220 mW term is a bound; later board revisions may use a different regulator. The board has no LiPo charger, and regulator dropout limits use near the end of charge.

Vendor product pages (Grepow, Adafruit, Pololu, Materialise, amesweb) are classed datasheet because the schema allows only datasheet or publication. Cited values were read on 2026-11-06 and are checked by sampling at the gate record; the ATI 304 sheet cited for the 304 parts is the same document read on 2026-11-06.
A2 screws are costed at 304 density (assumption).
Only two axial couplers are declared; no lateral side-face couplers, no branching or lattices. No through-coupler data or power contacts; power transfer is not provided.
